title: Korean Interference 2: /r/ vs /l/ — Print and Production

slides.teacher_cue: What sound? Tongue curls back — no contact with roof.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /r/ with tongue curled back, no contact.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution or Korean flap. Mirror work mandatory on every /r/ review.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound? Tongue tip touches the ridge just behind the upper front teeth.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /l/ with tongue tip contact at the alveolar ridge.
slides.correction_move: Model /l/ with mirror — tongue tip contact visible. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /r/ substitution (overcorrection) or Korean flap. Both /r/ and /l/ must be drilled from this lesson.

slides.teacher_cue: Quick review — sight word. Say it as a whole unit. Use it in a sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students say he immediately without blending.
slides.correction_move: Model he in a sentence, point to the underline, repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch for hesitation or blending attempts — sight word should be instant recognition.

slides.teacher_cue: Quick review — sight word. Say it as a whole unit. Use it in a sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students say me immediately without blending.
slides.correction_move: Model me in a sentence, point to the underline, repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch for hesitation or blending attempts — sight word should be instant recognition.

slides.teacher_cue: Play rot once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write rot accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay rot once, segment orally, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for r at onset — not l. Confirm /r/ production as students segment.

slides.teacher_cue: Play lip once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write lip accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay lip once, segment orally, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for l at onset — not r. Confirm /l/ tongue contact at ridge as students segment.

slides.teacher_cue: Play lock once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write lock accurately — note ck digraph.
slides.correction_move: Replay lock once, segment orally l-o-ck, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for l at onset — not r — and for correct ck spelling at coda.

content_payload.back_text: Two sounds. Two letters. Two different words.

slides.teacher_cue: Students have now learned BOTH r and l. From this lesson: EVERY /r/ word must be produced with /r/. Every /l/ word must be produced with /l/. Mirror work continues. Show printed card. Drill: r (curl) ... l (touch ridge) ... r ... l ... alternating 10 times.
slides.expected_response: Students alternate /r/ and /l/ production correctly and understand that both sounds are now in their reading inventory.
slides.correction_move: Mirror session: tongue curls for /r/, tip touches ridge for /l/. Alternate until students can switch cleanly.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students who still conflate both sounds. From this lesson, every r and l word in print must be read with the correct phoneme.

content_payload.correction_routine: This time correct answer is B — lip. /l/ — tongue touches ridge.

slides.teacher_cue: Which word is lip?
slides.expected_response: Students identify B (lip) as the /l/-onset word.
slides.correction_move: Play each word again. Contrast the onset positions. Students repeat lip three times with mirror.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ vs /r/ discrimination accuracy. Note students who still conflate the two.

slides.teacher_cue: Which word is lock?
slides.expected_response: Students identify A (lock) as the /l/-onset word.
slides.correction_move: Play each word again. Model /l/ tongue contact vs /r/ tongue curl. Students repeat lock three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for accurate discrimination between /l/ and /r/ when the vowel and coda are identical.

slides.teacher_cue: Which word is lot?
slides.expected_response: Students identify A (lot) as the /l/-onset word.
slides.correction_move: Play each word again. Model /l/ onset tongue position. Students repeat lot three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for accurate discrimination. Three minimal pairs back-to-back builds robust contrast.

slides.teacher_cue: Say rat. Tongue curls back for /r/ at onset — no contact. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rat with clean /r/ onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror, then model rat in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset — 'lat' for 'rat'.

slides.teacher_cue: Say rip. Tongue curls back for /r/ at onset — no contact. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rip with clean /r/ onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror, then model rip in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset — 'lip' for 'rip'. Note: lip is a real /l/ word.

slides.teacher_cue: Say rock. Tongue curls back for /r/ at onset — no contact. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rock with clean /r/ onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror, then model rock in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset — 'lock' for 'rock'. Note: lock is a real /l/ word.

slides.teacher_cue: Say lap. Tongue tip touches ridge for /l/ at onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say lap with clean /l/ onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model /l/ with mirror — tongue contact at ridge — then model lap in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /r/ substitution at onset (overcorrection) — 'rap' for 'lap'.

slides.teacher_cue: Say lip. Tongue tip touches ridge for /l/ at onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say lip with clean /l/ onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model /l/ with mirror — tongue contact at ridge — then model lip in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /r/ substitution at onset (overcorrection) — 'rip' for 'lip'.

slides.teacher_cue: Say lock. Tongue tip touches ridge for /l/ at onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say lock with clean /l/ onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model /l/ with mirror — tongue contact at ridge — then model lock in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /r/ substitution at onset (overcorrection) — 'rock' for 'lock'.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build rot left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build rot correctly: r | o | t.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of rot, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch that students place r first — not l.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build lot left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build lot correctly: l | o | t.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of lot, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch that students place l first — not r. Contrast this with rot from the previous slide.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build rip left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build rip correctly: r | i | p.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of rip, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch that students place r first — not l.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build lip left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build lip correctly: l | i | p.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of lip, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch that students place l first — not r. Contrast this with rip from the previous slide.

content_payload.text_content: A rat is on the rack.

slides.teacher_cue: A, the are sight words. All other words decodable. Two /r/-onset words: rat, rack.
slides.expected_response: Students read "A rat is on the rack." accurately with clean /r/ on rat and rack.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution on rat or rack.

content_payload.text_content: He can lock it. I got a rock.

slides.teacher_cue: He, I, a are sight words. All other words decodable. Mixed: lock (/l/ onset), rock (/r/ onset).
slides.expected_response: Students read both sentences accurately — /l/ on lock, /r/ on rock.
slides.correction_move: Model each sentence, then return to one-to-one word tracking. Contrast lock and rock if needed.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /r/ on lock (overcorrection) or /l/ on rock (interference). Both errors are possible here.

content_payload.text_content: The lip is on the rock. He ran to the lock.

slides.teacher_cue: The, the, He, to are sight words. All other words decodable. Mixed /r/ and /l/ onset words in the same sentences.
slides.expected_response: Students read both sentences accurately — /l/ on lip/lock, /r/ on rock/ran.
slides.correction_move: Model each sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking. Contrast each /r/ and /l/ word explicitly.
slides.observation_note: Watch for any phoneme swaps — especially lip vs rip, or lock vs rock — which are minimal pairs both in play here.

content_payload.text_content:
A rat ran.
He got a rock.
The rock is on a rack.
He can lock it.
I can rip the lip.
The rat ran to the lock.
content_payload.comprehension_prompt: What is on the rack? What can he lock?

slides.teacher_cue: Echo read first, then students read chorally. Point to each word. Ask the comprehension prompt after.
slides.expected_response: Students read all sentences accurately and answer the comprehension prompt.
slides.correction_move: Echo read line by line, then support each sentence before rereading the full passage.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /r/ vs /l/ accuracy throughout — every onset matters. Note any swaps between r/l pairs.

content_payload.text_content:
A rat ran.
He got a rock.
The rock is on a rack.
He can lock it.
I can rip the lip.
The rat ran to the lock.

slides.teacher_cue: Students reread the passage. Monitor /r/ vs /l/ distinction carefully — this pass is for fluency AND accuracy.
slides.expected_response: Students reread with improved fluency and consistent /r/ and /l/ production.
slides.correction_move: Pause and correct at the word level for any /r/ or /l/ error before continuing.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether /r/ vs /l/ accuracy holds or degrades under fluency demands.

content_payload.text_content: A rat ran. He got a rock. Lock it. Rip it.

slides.teacher_cue: Students take turns reading one sentence each. Monitor /r/ vs /l/ production throughout.
slides.expected_response: Students read each sentence with accurate /r/ and /l/ production on every onset word.
slides.correction_move: Pause and correct at the word level immediately for any /r/ or /l/ swap.
slides.observation_note: Watch for accuracy in partner reading — both /r/ and /l/ onset words are present. Note which students swap onsets.

slides.teacher_cue: Play rat once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write rat accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay rat once, segment orally, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for r at onset — not l — after the full contrast lesson.

slides.teacher_cue: Play lock once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write lock accurately — note ck digraph.
slides.correction_move: Replay lock once, segment orally l-o-ck, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for l at onset — not r — and correct ck spelling at coda.

slides.teacher_cue: Play rock once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write rock accurately — note ck digraph.
slides.correction_move: Replay rock once, segment orally r-o-ck, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for r at onset — not l. Contrast with lock from the previous slide: both end in -ock but differ at onset.

slides.teacher_cue: Which word is lack?
slides.expected_response: Students identify B (lack) as the /l/-onset word.
slides.correction_move: Play each word again. Model /l/ tongue contact vs /r/ tongue curl. Students repeat lack three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for accurate /l/ vs /r/ discrimination at lesson close — consolidation check.

content_payload.support_text: Top row: /r/ words. Bottom row: /l/ words. Say each pair. Feel the difference.

slides.teacher_cue: Students say each word. Feel the contrast between /r/ (curl) and /l/ (touch ridge) across paired words.
slides.expected_response: Students produce each word with the correct onset phoneme — /r/ on rat, rock, rip and /l/ on lap, lot, lip.
slides.correction_move: For any onset error, isolate the onset, mirror the tongue position, and have student re-attempt the full word.
slides.observation_note: Watch for production consistency across all six words — both /r/ and /l/ onsets under pressure.

content_payload.title: Close the Lesson

check_items.label: Say rock and lock. What is the difference at the start?
Which of these starts with /l/: rat, lip, rack, rip?
Say one sentence using a word that starts with /l/ and one that starts with /r/.

content_payload.notes_field: Check: can students reliably distinguish /r/ and /l/ in both speech and print? Note any students who still need mirror work.

slides.teacher_cue: Close with contrast recall, discrimination check, and two oral transfer sentences.
slides.expected_response: Students articulate the /r/-/l/ distinction, identify the /l/-onset word correctly, and produce two sentences with the target onsets.
slides.correction_move: Return to mirror work for any student who cannot articulate the difference. Model one sentence per phoneme if needed.
slides.observation_note: Watch for whether students can name the distinction and apply it in spontaneous oral production.
